text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: paging sam (on-call) — SLO breach: cont-batching p99 latency (streaming) > 5s for the last 12m. Auto-escalation to eng-runtime if not acknowledged in 5m. link: https://redwood.internal/ops/incidents/1879001234

sam: ack — I'm on it. seeing the alert in pagerduty and cloudwatch. starting triage.

jess: copying logs from the alert: 
```
metric: contbatch.streaming.p99 = 5.8s (baseline 1.1s)
metric: contbatch.streams_in_flight spikes at 420
metric: streaming_stalls_detected: 74 (last 15m)
reason_tag: mixed_seqlen_queueing
```

sam: initial hypothesis — continuous batching scheduler is accumulating long sequences behind short ones causing KV cache thrash + preemption. p95 also creeping up but p99 is worst.

kai: can you grab a hot-request example id? need an example to reproduce and check KV cache miss ratio.

sam: pulling trace for req id 9a7c3f2b. attaching head of trace: 
```
trace 9a7c3f2b: enqueue(0.0s) -> batch_wait(0.8s) -> start_exec(0.8s) -> stream_send stall(3.2s) -> finish(4.0s)
kv_cache_miss_ratio: 0.67 for that batch
batch_size: 18 (target max 64), effective seq-len spread: min 16 max 2048
```

praveen: 0.67 miss ratio is high. looks like large seqs forcing long kernel runs while many small ones wait. scheduler fairness is not preempting long-running batches.

eng-runtime: pinging in. we have a quick mitigation matrix: (1) disable continuous batching for streaming routes (2) cap batch_size or prefer sequence-length aware packing (3) fallback routing to standard non-continuous path (4) throttling / shed lower tier traffic.

sam: short-term: recommend turning off cont-batching for streaming model: `rbctl routes update --route streaming-v2 --continuous-batching=false` — low-risk and reversible. I'll test on staging first.

jess: agree. staging flip (rbctl) shows p99 back to 1.3s for same workload. staging run: 
```
# staging
rbctl metrics query --route streaming-v2 --window 10m p99
result: 1.3s
```

kai: ok - plan for prod: run the flip on 2x servesets (us-east-1a/b) to avoid full-region hit, monitor for error increase. also prepare temporary rate limit: `--burst 100 --rate 50r/s` for free-tier customers to protect prod.

sam: executing prod change in 3m. will start on us-east-1a then wait 60s then us-east-1b. tagging cs-ops for customer comms.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: change started by sam — change-id=chg-187900A; CI checks passed; will apply to target serveset us-east-1a.

sam: applied to us-east-1a. monitoring...

10:31 sam: p99 down to 2.1s (partial). stalls count reduced to 22.

10:33 sam: applied to us-east-1b.

10:34 jess: p99=1.4s region-wide. streaming_stalls_detected=6. KV miss ratio dropped to 0.12. :thumbsup:

cs-ops: noted customer-facing impact matrix: about ~1.2% of streaming requests (product analytics) experienced >5s lat prior to mitigation. We're preparing a concise note for affected customers with context and mitigation steps.

praveen: follow-up engineering actions: 
- add seq-length aware packing policy for cont-batching (short-term knob)
- implement preemptive fairness: split batches if a long-tail item detected (medium-term)
- add a metric for batch-seq-spread and alert when > threshold (immediate)

kai: I'll open a RFC for scheduler fairness change and include perf tests. I want to run a synthetic that mixes seq lengths 10:1 with ratio 300:1 to validate.

eng-runtime: logging runbook updates: 
- on SLO breach p99 for streaming, first mitigation: disable cont-batching for affected route (safe rollback)
- second: apply rate-limits / tier-based shedding if customer impact continues
- alert owner to schedule follow-up postmortem within 48h and notify product + CS

sam: handoff to next on-call (jess) at 11:00 UTC. summary for handoff: 
- root cause: cont-batching scheduler + mixed sequence lengths causing long-running kernel tasks and KV cache misses -> tail latency
- mitigation applied: cont-batching disabled on streaming-v2 across prod (us-east). batch_size cap experiment rolled out on baseline routes.
- customer impact: ~1.2% of streaming requests >5s for ~12m window. no data loss. CS outreach in flight (ticket INC-187900).
- next actions: implement seq-aware packing, add batch-seq-spread metric/alert, RFC for fairness and preemption, run regression evals.

jess: ack and taking over handoff. I'll coordinate with praveen to prioritize seq-aware packing in the next sprint and set a follow-up meeting. tagging @praveen.

praveen: thanks — I'll also scope a short-term scheduler knob (max_long_seq_runtime_ms) so we can auto-shed/isolated long seqs if they exceed runtime.

sam: closing page. incident-bot: please mark incident resolved if metrics stay stable for 30m.

incident-bot: noted. marking resolved-provisional. created incident ticket INC-187900 and postmortem stub: https://redwood.internal/ops/incidents/INC-187900/postmortem

jess: quick note for the postmortem: include the load test that reproduces mixing ratio, add graphs of KV miss ratio pre/ post mitigation, and document customer comms timeline.

eng-runtime: added a dashboard panel for `batch_seq_spread` and `kv_cache_miss_ratio` and a short alert runbook.

cs-ops: will publish customer note template and send to affected accounts in next 2 hours.

jess: thanks everyone. I'll keep monitoring for 2h and then file the full postmortem. :eyes:
